headline: National Seashore Entry and Parking Verification
reservation: Entry to the town is public, but parking at Cape Cod National Seashore beaches like Race Point requires a daily fee or pass during the summer season. Ferries from Boston and local guesthouses often sell out months in advance; always check the official NPS site for changing access to the Province Lands Visitor Center.

days.title: Maritime History and Town Heights

stops.name: Pilgrim Monument
stops.detail: Climb the granite tower for a 360-degree view of the Cape's 'hook' and the surrounding Atlantic.

stops.name: Commercial Street
stops.detail: Walk the vibrant center of town to explore historic art galleries, seafood markets, and 19th-century architecture.

days.driving: Local walking; no vehicle needed for town center.
days.note: Commercial Street is extremely narrow; biking or walking is the most efficient way to navigate during the day.

days.title: Dunes and Atlantic Surf
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Bike Barn

stops.name: Province Lands Bike Trail
stops.detail: Cycle the 5.5-mile loop through the sand dunes and pine forests of the National Seashore.

stops.name: Race Point Beach
stops.detail: Visit the tip of the Cape to watch for seals and explore the historic Life-Saving Station.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes by bike or shuttle; conditions vary.
days.note: Biking the dunes involves steep grades; check your rental's brakes and carry plenty of water for the sun-exposed route.

days.title: Marine Giants and Forest Trails

stops.name: Stellwagen Bank National Marine Sanctuary
stops.detail: Join a sanctioned whale watching tour to spot humpback and fin whales in their primary feeding grounds.

stops.name: Beech Forest Trail
stops.detail: Walk the shaded freshwater pond loop, a prime location for birdwatching and a contrast to the salt marshes.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes to the trailhead; conditions vary.
days.note: Whale watch tours are weather-dependent; check for cancellations at the pier on the morning of departure.

intel.title: Town vs. Seashore Lots
intel.text: Municipal lots at MacMillan Pier use a kiosk system and fill by 11 AM in summer. National Seashore lots at Herring Cove and Race Point require a separate federal fee collected at the gate.

intel.title: Harbor and Dune Coverage
intel.text: Cell service is reliable within the town limits but can be intermittent among the high dunes of the Province Lands. Download the NPS Cape Cod app for offline trail navigation.

intel.title: Outer Cape Logistics
intel.text: Fuel stations are located along Route 6 in North Truro and Wellfleet; services within Provincetown proper are limited and can be difficult to access with an RV. Stock up on mainland supplies before crossing the Canal.

intel.title: Ferry and Bridge Traffic
intel.text: The high-speed ferry from Boston takes 90 minutes but is prone to sea-state delays. Driving Route 6 on summer Fridays can double the travel time from Hyannis due to heavy bridge traffic.

intel.title: Seasonal Shuttle Services
intel.text: A seasonal shuttle connects the town center to the beaches and North Truro campgrounds, reducing the need for a car. Check the current season's schedule for the latest stop locations and hours.

plan.arrival: Arrive via ferry or Route 6; park in the long-term municipal lot and use the local shuttle or a bike to reach your guesthouse.
plan.vehicle: A car is often a liability in the narrow town streets; a bicycle is the preferred regional transport. RVs should be parked at designated North Truro campgrounds rather than driven into the town center.
plan.goldenHour: Herring Cove Beach is the rare East Coast location where the sun appears to set over the water; check seasonal angles for the best view.
